Vice Chairman, Non-Insurance Operations, and director

background_rationale: Trained and worked as an accountant at PricewaterhouseCoopers before joining a client, CalEnergy, and rising through the energy business that became Berkshire Hathaway Energy.

notable.summary: Ahead of taking over as CEO, Berkshire announced a leadership reshuffle naming Nancy Pierce CEO of GEICO, Adam Johnson head of consumer products, service and retailing, Charles Chang as next CFO, and a new general counsel role.
In his first annual shareholder letter, Abel pledged to preserve Berkshire's culture and values and said he wants the company to be stronger 20 years from now.
Berkshire repurchased about $234 million of its own stock in March 2026, its first buybacks in roughly 21 months.
Hosting his first annual meeting as CEO, Abel said Berkshire would not be broken up and that it would be patient in deploying its record cash position of about $380 billion.

personal_story.hook: As a boy in Edmonton, Greg Abel cleaned discarded bottles for refund money; he went on to succeed Warren Buffett as CEO.
personal_story.summary: Abel was born in 1962 in Edmonton, Alberta, and grew up in a working-class neighborhood. As a boy he delivered advertising flyers and cleaned discarded bottles for redemption money, and in high school and college he filled fire extinguishers and worked as a laborer for a forest products company. He took extra exams to get into the University of Alberta, lived at home to save money, and graduated with a commerce degree with distinction in 1984. He joined PricewaterhouseCoopers in Edmonton, moved to its San Francisco office, and then went to work for one of his clients, CalEnergy, the start of a path through MidAmerican and Berkshire Hathaway Energy that led to Berkshire's top job in 2026.

open_issues: Degree: Horatio Alger and Yahoo/Canadian Press say commerce degree; Wikipedia says bachelor's in accounting. Recorded degree as BCom with field Accounting; field unconfirmed by an official source.
PwC office: Wikipedia says he started at PwC in San Francisco; Horatio Alger says Edmonton first, then San Francisco. Start/end years 1984-1992 inferred from graduation and CalEnergy join date.

MidAmerican presidency date differs: Horatio Alger says 1999, Canadian Press says 1998; Canadian Press also implies he became CEO around 2000, while Horatio Alger says CEO in 2008. Used 1999 and 2008.
Father's occupation differs: Wikipedia says he manufactured firefighting equipment; Horatio Alger says salesman. Omitted from story.
Wikipedia names hockey player Sid Abel as a relative; not independently verified, omitted.
